title: Failed update rollback can restore a revoked light node's report credential
description: Source supports a sequence where a light node is deleted during target verification and failed-update rollback restores its pre-update host record and reporting secret. Whether the restored panel then accepts a fresh report from a dummy revoked node and updates telemetry remains unobserved.
claimed_root_cause: Rollback restores the pre-update panel data directory as a whole, so it can overwrite an authorized light-node revocation made during target-release verification without reapplying that revocation.

trace.description: The update preparer stops the agent and panel writers before archiving their data.
Compose starts the target panel before target readiness is checked and the transaction is completed.
A cluster mutation request can invoke light-host deletion during target verification.
The store removes the host record from persisted state and then deletes its reporting credential file.
A failed or interrupted verification path restores automatic-update data.
The restore exchanges the live panel directory for the one extracted from the transaction snapshot.
Light-report authentication loads the current host record and stored secret, then checks request freshness and the HMAC.
An accepted light report updates the host telemetry snapshot.

evidence.description: The transaction archives data/panel and data/agent after stopping the writers and verifies the archive checksum.
The target Compose panel starts before readiness and transaction completion checks at lines 1937–1938.
The cluster-host delete handler invokes the cluster service deletion operation after its mutation checks.
Deleting a light host removes its persisted record; lines 565–568 remove its light and terminal credentials.
Restore moves the current panel data directory aside and moves the snapshot directory into its place; it does not merge post-snapshot changes.
Authentication computes and compares the HMAC using the secret loaded for the current host record.
A successfully authenticated report is persisted as the host's new telemetry snapshot.
The fixture asserts that a preseeded light-node credential file still contains node-secret after rollback; it does not exercise report authentication after host-record deletion.

blockers: The task prohibits running the target, tests, fixtures, or Docker without a parent-approved OS-enforced sandbox. Source review cannot establish whether rollback restores an executable light store that accepts a fresh dummy-node report and updates telemetry.

validation_plan.local: In an approved offline OS-enforced sandbox, use a temporary data directory and a synthetic light-host record with a generated dummy HMAC key. Snapshot the data, start the target panel, delete the dummy host during readiness verification, force readiness failure, run rollback, then submit a fresh signed report to the restored prior panel. Observe whether authentication succeeds and telemetry changes.
